summary: Practise IFRS 9 staging, ECL calculations, overlays, and disclosures with lending cases. Explore the five-day course and review the syllabus.
lede: IFRS 9 expected credit loss training covers how finance and credit-risk professionals prepare and explain impairment estimates. It develops skills in staging and significant increase in credit risk decisions, portfolio segmentation, PD/LGD/EAD-based calculations, forward-looking scenario weighting, and documenting overlays and model validation. Spreadsheet-based lending casework lets participants practise creating an evidence trail and reconciling estimates with IFRS 7 disclosures.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who prepare, review, govern, or report IFRS 9 impairment estimates across lending portfolios. This course is designed for: Bank impairment managers overseeing ECL close processes and provision approval. Microfinance finance managers reconciling loan-loss estimates to financial statements. SACCO credit-risk analysts monitoring arrears, SICR indicators, and portfolio migration. IFRS 9 model analysts estimating PD, LGD, EAD, and scenario impacts. Credit-risk model validators challenging assumptions, segmentation, and model limitations. Financial controllers reviewing impairment journals and IFRS 7 disclosure reconciliations. Internal auditors testing ECL governance, approvals, and model-change records. External reporting specialists preparing expected-credit-loss notes and supporting schedules. Portfolio credit officers supplying borrower and arrears data for staging assessments. Finance transformation leads coordinating digital ECL workflows and reporting controls.
prerequisites: Prior working knowledge of financial reporting and lending or credit-risk operations is expected. Familiarity with loan portfolios, impairment processes, and spreadsheet calculations will help you complete the case exercises. No coding or programming is required; exercises use Excel-based calculations and templates.
